chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqa, from Ammar al-Sabati, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the limit of the clay in which one does not prostrate; what is it? He said: 'When the forehead sinks and does not remain firm upon the ground.'

And regarding the man who prays between the graves, he said: 'That is not permissible unless he places between himself and the graves, when he prays, ten cubits in front of him, and ten cubits behind him, and ten cubits to his right, and ten cubits to his left. Then he prays if he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: What is the required distance from graves when praying, and how deep must clay be for valid prostration?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies two practical aspects of prayer validity: it establishes that clay must be firm enough to support the forehead without sinking excessively, ensuring physical stability during sujdah, and it permits praying near graves provided a sufficient ten-cubit clearance is maintained on all sides to avoid distraction or disrespect. These rulings reflect the Shia scholarly emphasis on both the physical conditions of the prayer surface and the spatial context of the worshipper, balancing ritual purity with practical accessibility in varied environments.
